previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of morbid obesity, type 2 diabetes, diastolic heart failure, polymyositis, and chronic anticoagulation for recurrent DVT/PE was admitted with right upper thigh pain and fever. She was found to have a cutaneous abscess that was initially drained in the emergency department. Due to persistent pain and imaging confirmation of a residual fluid collection, she underwent a second ultrasound-guided drainage. Cultures from the abscess grew Proteus mirabilis, and her antibiotics were narrowed from intravenous vancomycin and Zosyn to oral ciprofloxacin. Her warfarin was continued throughout with a therapeutic INR at discharge, though she was counseled on potential interaction with ciprofloxacin requiring close INR monitoring at home. Her other chronic conditions remained stable. She improved clinically, completed necessary procedures, and was discharged home with a plan to finish a 7-day course of antibiotics, follow up with her primary care provider, and monitor her INR.

Brief summary of hospital course:
=================================
___ year old female with past medical history of asthma, 
polymyositis with ILD, dCHF, recurrent PE/DVTs (on warfarin), 
DM2, OSA, and HTN who presents with chief complaint of shortness 
of breath, cough, and malaise. She was not hypoxic. She was 
started on duo nebs, and 60 mg of p.o. prednisone for a total of 
5-day course and discharge on a prednisone taper. She was also 
treated for a mild CHF exacerbation, receiving IV Lasix for 
diuresis. Although the patient has a history of interstitial 
lung disease, the shortness of breath was not felt to be 
secondary to the ILD. On discharge, she was reportedly improving 
in her subjective sensation of breathing though states that she 
needs oxygen to help her throat closing sensation, her vital 
signs were within normal limits, and she was discharged on the 
same medications she started on while inpatient.

# Asthma exacerbation
# Dyspnea 
This process was seemed to be caused by the patient's multiple 
pulmonary comorbidities, specifically her ILD, asthma, CHF, OSA, 
and obesity hypoventilation syndrome, all which cause poor 
pulmonary reserve, though with likely asthma exacerbation. 
During hospital stay, she was not hypoxic. She had been treated 
with duo nebs and received a course of steroids for an asthma 
exacerbation based on ___ flow rates measured in the emergency 
department. Her breathing subjectively improved. She was 
discharged on 60mg daily of prednisone tapering 10mg every 3 
days until back to her home dose of prednisone. On the day of 
discharge, the patient reported subjective improvement in her 
breathing, though was afraid of leaving the hospital as she 
states that she needs oxygen to help her throat closing 
sensation. She would benefit from outpatient pulmonary follow 
up. 

# Polymyositis with pulmonary involvement
# ILD
We did not believe she was having a flair of her polymyositis. 
Her pred burst for asthma exacerbation was written for a taper 
on discharge to her home dose of 10 mg.

# Chronic ___
Exam is very difficult. BNP was only mildly elevated. CXR read 
with mild pulmonary edema, but when diuresed with IV Lasix, Cr 
increased. She triggered for tachypnea without desaturation and 
tachypnea was thought to be secondary to panic attack versus 
worsening exacerbation. She was discharged on her home torsemide 
of 10mg daily. Would recommend follow up.

regular checks of your INR.  Please arrange for these regular 
checks as you have done previously.
 - Please make a follow up appointment with your PULMONOLOGIST 
to follow up your interstitial lung disease and possible asthma 
exacerbation.
